text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own — in municipal senior management, male-dominated panels are common enough to be unremarkable. Treated as your headline argument, it looks speculative and puts people on the defensive.

The stronger facts are the credential gap (master's, licence, 12 years versus a bachelor's) and the vague, non-comparable rationale about consultation experience. Pursue those first: send a follow-up requesting the written reasons, the scoring criteria and your scores against the successful candidate's.

Mention panel composition only as context if the reasons come back thin or shift after the fact — it corroborates a pattern, it doesn't establish one.
